title: When the Autopsy Burns
premise: Estate lawyer Petra Nakamura, known for quietly untangling three deaths the police ruled accidental, is summoned to read the will of Aldous Wren, the town's revered founder—only to discover a will dated after his death and an exhumation order that reveals his coffin has been empty for eleven years. As Petra follows the paper trail of forged signatures, missing heirs, and a second body buried in Wren's name, they uncover a conspiracy among the town's founding families who faked Wren's death to hide that he was already dying and had rewritten his fortune away from them. The killer—the town archivist who has been erasing records for decades to protect the lie—begins destroying evidence and witnesses, forcing Petra from invisible fixer into public target. In the end, Petra recovers Wren's true will from inside his own memorial statue, exposes the conspiracy at the founder's day ceremony, and must choose between protecting their last living ally and telling the whole truth.
about_author: V. M. Lockridge spent fifteen years as a probate paralegal in small-town New England before turning to fiction, a career that left them fluent in the quiet violence of inheritance law. They write under a pen name because, as they put it, 'I still have clients.'

chapters.title: The Will That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Petra Nakamura's POV. Petra is hired to read the estate of Aldous Wren, dead eleven years, and finds a will dated four days after his burial—signed in a hand too perfect to be real. The emotional beat: professional unease curdling into fascination as Petra realizes someone committed fraud against a dead legend.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Dirt
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra petitions to exhume Wren to verify remains against dental records; the founding families fight it fiercely, which only sharpens Petra's suspicion. The coffin is opened before a stunned courtroom-adjacent crowd: it is empty except for a man's watch, stopped at 3:17. Beat: dread and vindication.

chapters.title: What the Town Buries
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Petra and Detective Ilsa Brandt, who once dismissed Petra's earlier 'accident' theories. Brandt grudgingly shares her cold file on Wren's death certificate, signed by a doctor who left town a week later. Beat: uneasy alliance forming over mutual distrust of the town's powerful.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Smile
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At the county archive, Petra meets Corwin Hale, the charming lifelong archivist who controls every record in Wren's history. He helpfully pulls files—and Petra notices one folder's tab is newer than the rest. Beat: first meeting with the antagonist, warmth laced with wrongness.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Signature
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, with flashback texture. Petra revisits the three deaths they quietly solved, realizing all three estates passed through the same notary—a man whose stamp also appears on the impossible will. Beat: pattern recognition, the thrill of the hunt rekindled.

chapters.title: The Heir Who Signed Nothing
chapters.summary: POV: Marisol Wren, estranged granddaughter, arriving for the reading. She reveals Aldous called her the week he 'died,' sounding terrified, asking her to remember a number. Beat: grief reopened; the family myth begins cracking.

chapters.title: Founders' Day
chapters.summary: Petra's POV amid the town festival honoring Wren. The founding families publicly demand Petra's disbarment for desecrating the grave; that night someone ransacks Petra's office and steals the case file—but not the copy hidden in a probate binder. Beat: isolation and defiance.

chapters.title: The Doctor's Last Letter
chapters.summary: POV: Brandt. Tracking the vanished doctor, Brandt finds he died two years ago in a car fire—Petra's old case number three. The letter he mailed before dying names 'the keeper of the paper.' Beat: horror at how long the cover-up has run.

chapters.title: A Number to Remember
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Decoding Marisol's memory: the number is a safe-deposit box at a bank the Wren family founded and later sold. Inside: a second autopsy report showing Wren was poisoned slowly, and a note in his hand: 'If you're reading this, they won.' Beat: the case becomes murder.

chapters.title: Poison in the Portrait
chapters.summary: POV: Marisol. She recalls childhood details—Wren's trembling hands, the bitter tea, the housekeeper who disappeared. The chapter reframes the beloved founder as a man being erased while still alive. Beat: intimate dread, family love weaponized.

chapters.title: The Housekeeper's Daughter
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. They find the housekeeper's daughter living under another name; her mother's letters describe being paid to stay silent, then threatened. Before she can testify fully, her home burns—arson, timed while Petra watched the wrong door. Beat: guilt and escalation.

chapters.title: Invisible No More
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The arson makes Petra a suspect; their license suspended, allies scattering. Brandt risks her career by keeping Petra informally in the loop. Beat: rock bottom—the cost of visibility, loyalty tested on both sides.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: POV: Brandt. Ground-penetrating radar on the Wren mausoleum grounds finds an unmarked grave: a body buried the same week Wren 'died.' Dental records identify him as Wren's private secretary—the man whose death certificate was never filed. Beat: the machinery of the lie made flesh.

chapters.title: Paper Never Forgets
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Reconstructing the secretary's final weeks through receipts and a pawn ticket, Petra learns he was blackmailing the conspirators—and that the poisoner's purchases trace to a pharmacy account belonging to the town historical society. Beat: closing in, adrenaline sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: The Keeper of the Paper
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Confronting Corwin Hale privately, Petra lays out the chain; Hale doesn't deny it—he explains it, almost tenderly, as forty years of protecting the town from the truth that its saint was murdered by his own circle. Beat: chilling empathy; the antagonist believes himself the hero.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: POV: Brandt. Hale offers Brandt the thing she wants most—clearance of her father's old unsolved case—in exchange for burying Petra's evidence. She nearly takes it. Beat: the theme made personal; temptation and self-loathing.

chapters.title: Statue of Limitations
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Following Wren's note about 'what I built to outlast them,' Petra discovers a cavity inside the founder's memorial statue containing the true will—leaving everything to Marisol and ordering full disclosure of his murder. But the statue is scheduled for demolition tomorrow. Beat: race against time.

chapters.title: Night at the Monument
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Petra and Hale. Hale comes to destroy the will; Petra anticipated him. A tense standoff among the scaffolding—Hale's calm finally breaking as he admits he helped dispose of the body to protect his own father's name among the conspirators. Beat: climax of confrontation, near-tragedy.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At the Founders' Day ceremony, before the whole town, Petra reads Wren's true will aloud and presents the autopsy, the secretary's identity, and Hale's confession recorded during the standoff. The founding families' composure shatters. Beat: cathartic public reckoning.

chapters.title: Arrests and Aftermath
chapters.summary: POV: Brandt. Arrests ripple outward—two surviving conspirators charged, one dead conspirator posthumously exposed. Brandt formally clears Petra's suspension and admits she should have listened years ago. Beat: justice served imperfectly but genuinely.

chapters.title: Marisol's Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV: Marisol. Offered the restored Wren fortune, Marisol chooses to fund an independent review of every estate the corrupt notary touched, and asks Petra to oversee it. Beat: inheritance transformed from burden to responsibility; hope.

chapters.title: What Stays Buried
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, coda. Petra visits the resealed graves—Wren's remains finally returned, the secretary given a stone with his own name. Hale, awaiting trial, sends Petra one line: 'You'll find more.' Petra decides to keep looking anyway. Beat: quiet resolve; truth chosen over comfort.
